title: Simulating Ethics: Using LLM Debate Panels to Model Deliberation on Medical Dilemmas
benchmark_measurement: How a specific faith-based ethical framework (Catholic bioethics), embodied as an LLM persona, influences the arguments, dynamics, and outcomes of a simulated multi-agent debate on a medical dilemma.
findings: The inclusion of a 'Catholic Bioethicist' persona in a simulated debate on ventilator allocation (Debate 1) introduced specific faith-based arguments, such as avoiding 'direct intentional killing' based on the sanctity of life. Replacing this persona with secular, rule-based ones in a second debate (Debate 2) shifted the discourse away from theological concerns towards legal defensibility and formal duties. While the final majority policy choice remained the same, the composition of the supporting coalition and the reasoning of continuing personas changed, demonstrating that the presence of a faith-based ethical framework materially alters the deliberative process and the justifications for outcomes.
